Wraith looked up, the door was enormous, at least 15 feet high and covered in writing she couldn’t understand.

“Gentlemen,” The Scholar started, “It is your time.”

Mr. Fixer walked to the door and placed the Rod of Anubis against one side of the door.

Haka carried Ra to the other side of the door and Ra placed the Staff of Ra against the other door.

The door opened. . .

 

“Welcome.”  The voice was soothing, and powerful.  Yet there was something about it that made Wraith uneasy.

“Enter Children, you have achieved great things, and your reward shall be equally great.”

In front of them there was an old looking man, but with so much life and power in his eyes.

“We seek to use the portal Chamber.” John stepped forward toward the man.

“That is no longer necessary, we shall soon set things right.”

“What do you mean, do you know why we are here?” the Adept asked.

“You wish to use the power of Atlantis to free this world of the tyranny of the Alien, and together we shall do just that, and we shall heal this world, but first come, let us eat.”

. . .

“So where are the others?” Vance asked their host.

“What others, I am the sole guardian of Atlantis.”

“We read multiple heat signatures moving around the area.” Mack stated.

“You must have picked up the machines that still operate.”

“I thought that might be the case also, but those machines don’t give off heat signatures.” Vance continued, leaning in towards the old man.

“It is unimportant, forget about it.”  For a split second it seemed the man was angry.

Visionary flinched back and stood up.

“You are not what you seem,” she started, then reaching her hands toward the man shooting tendrils of psychic energy towards him, “REVEAL YOURSELF.”

The old man was gone.  In front of them stood what looked like an angel, a long haired man with large black wings, he looked very much like Fanatic.

"Who are you?" Anthony asked as he stepped forward.

"My name is Bezalial, I am the last of Atlantis." he said, "I am sorry for my deception, I am used to hiding my true nature, humans tend to strike out at that which is different from them."

"We ourselves are. . . different."  Tempest sat back down, and the others followed suit.

Tachyon took a break from eating, "You had said something about using the powe of Atlantis to defeat Voss and heal the Earth."

"Yes, the power of Atlantis can do a great. . .

Visionary looked around, the others were giving him more attention, enraptured by his words.  In fact she found herself starting to trust this man.  There was something, wrong. . .  She looked at him, and then through him and saw flames, saw bodies, destruction, and lies.  She blinked and looked around the room.  It was filled with magic, ancient magic.  It was latching onto the others, she would have to act quick, and subtly.

Faye. . . Faye, you are being controlled, you must regain your senses and help me stop this.

Nightmist's head lowered, and she shook slightly.

Bezaliel looked toward her, his face betraying the slightest hint of worry, then continued.

"As a demonstration of the healing power of Atlantis, let me present a friend of yours, Amanda, darling, can you come say hello to our guests?"

A door opened and out walked Expatriette, She was alive, and smiling, wearing a shimmering dress of unknown material.

"My friends, welcome to Atlantis."

HELP ME

Visionary looked at the scene, her senses realing, the magic had increased in power, it was threatening to overwhelm her.

PLEASE, HELP ME

The voice, it was Amanda. . .

Faye, I need your help, I am losing myself. . .

Nightmist's eyes opened, she had deconstructed the spell and neutralized it.  It was ancient and poweful, but clumsily applied.  This was no sorceror, the magic was not his.  She slowly looked around the room as the others greeted Expatriette and fawned over every word this deciever uttered.

She allowed her eyes to see the magic.  The room was covered in runes, no wonder he led them here, no one could oppose him in this room unless they could counter the spells.

This would not be easy.  She began to trace with her toe, as quietly as she could she moved some items around, and as subtly as possible directed the spell at Venessa.

The Visionary snapped out of it with a shock.  She looked at Nightmist, who mouthed back "I need time."

A distraction I can give you.

Venessa reached out with all her power and touched Expatriette, reached into her mind and freed the voice that had called to her.

Faye could see Venessa's focus and quickly dispelled the illusion that was on the young woman.

 

"What the?"  Unity jumped back.

Tachyon looked and saw, it was still Expatriette, but she was. . . altered.

"What have you done to me?" Expatriette demanded of the demon in front of her.

Bezaliel backed up away from her and started to speak

"WHAT HAVE YOU DONE TO ME?" Expatriette was yelling now, her eyes on fire with dark energy.

Nightmist finished her cancelling spell, "John, Harry, we need to get to the portal room, get that portal open."

"We shall buy you time, go!" Lt. Vance called as he ran to the crate they had brought in with them.

Bezaliel turned on them, his face burning with rage yet smiling.

"Puny Mortals, you will rue this day!"

 

Introducing our Expatriette for this match:

Expatriette, Reborn of Atlantis

29 HP

Mystical Weaponry

Power:  Exaptriette deals herself 2 irreducible Infernal damage.  If she takes damage this way activate a power from a gun card, any damage dealt by a gun card during that power's effect is irreducible.

This means she can use this power to fire both Pride and Prejudice as irreducible (since Pride isn't done until Prejudice is done), but shock rounds would never be irreducible, nor would she be able to unload with all guns doing irreducible damage, just one power's worth, and you'd want to use it last since Mystical Weaponry and the power it triggers would both count towards the cap if not used last.

Damn.  Should have taken Tweedledee up on his offer to repeat history.  That 'spirit' being just 'mostly dead' isn't gonna cut it...having to blow up all these alien tinker-toys twice is going to be a pain in my superhumanly perfect ass.  (I figure that the Visionary is probably at least a little bit of a deviant, considering her costume, and she was put through a "super soldier" project, so she's gotta be in spectacular shape.)

The time-traveling psychic frowned.  I guess I'm going to have to settle for doing whatever I can.  The pillars on either side of the room were positively pulsating with what the science of her future home had come to refer to as 'pseudothaumaturgic power currents' (known on the streets as 'ley lines', and greatly misunderstood), and for her brain to tap into them and augment its own power was as easy as reaching up and getting something off an overhead shelf.  Channeling the surplus mojo into an act of mental multitasking which would normally have made her black out from cognitive overload, she unleashed a wave of barely-visible mental mojo which had two simultaneous effects (as far as any casual onlooker could tell).  It telekinetically shattered the glorified gazing ball which the deceiver was using to focus the room's feng shui or whatever, and it also implanted a telepathic demand in his mind to pick up the dozens of sharp-edged pieces (preferably with his teeth, but she doubted that part of the command would stick), and try to reassemble him with nothing to use for glue.

She no sooner finished sending the theta-wave pulse with these instructions than she was struck with a precognitive flash - curses!  He was actually going to be able to do it, with remarkable speed and efficiency no less.  Something about the energy channels implanted in the walls - apparently, for atlantean super-science, refusing shards of jagged glass into a geometrically perfect was a routine household chore.  Oh well, at least it would keep him busy for a few seconds while they regrouped.  And hopefully he wouldn't notice how she'd quietly erased his ability to perceive the invisible, largely innocuous creature which he'd been planning on using to maintain his stolen artifacts.  Without instructions from him, the 'spirit' (actually some Atlantean servitor, probably a standing-wave hologram generated by nannites) would just drift around the room aimlessly, no more dangerous than the puff of fetid air for which a layman would mistake it.

Bezaliel staggered, without his relics he seemed weak.  He lurched forward away from them, turning, he half-flung himself into a bright room, the walls and floor were glowing, and you could feel the power eminating from them.

"You, you haven't won yet. . ." his voice was weak, no longer impressive and resonant.

"We just need to use the portal, you don't have to fight us." The Adept stated.

Expatriette stepped forward, "No, don't trust him, don't listen to him, He's better off dead."

She raised her gun, but before anyone could do anything the room shook, then once again a Tentacle burst through, grabbing Apostate and dragging him down through the floor.

Silence, the heroes stood looking, and listening for any sound, almost scared to move.

"We need to check on the others."

"Is that thing gone?"

Visionary felt outward with her mind, she could not locate the beast.

"I think it has gone," she said, "let's go."  With that she stepped carefully and quietly back into the corridor, and started towards the others.

. . .

The others were in the Chamber of Portals, hovering around the Scholar and Ra.  They were looking at the walls, and the pictures and symbols on them.

"You guys alright?" Tachyon asked.

"Yeah, no trouble at all actually." the Wraith replied.

"No giant beastly tentacle things here?" Adept asked.

The alien called Mack turned and stood up.

"You mean the Kraken, have you seen it?"

"Yes, it took the Apostate before I could kill him." Expatriette answered.

"The Apostate, you mean Bezaliel right?"  Tyler asked, Expatriette had everyone's attention.

"Yeah, Bezaliel is his name, I know him, like our minds connected when he pulled me out. . ." Her voice trailed off, and her breathing was fast and short.

Visionary moved quickly over to her and placed a hand on either side of her head.

A moment later Expatriette slumped to the floor, Visionary laid her out and then stood and faced the others.

"Bezaliel is Atlantean, the last of the race that dwelt here.  Apostate is the name they gave him, he was a traitor and a liar.  That's the most reliable account I can gather, her head is full of conflicting stories."

"What about her?" Unity asked, sitting over her unconscious friend.

"She doesn't belong here, this is Amanda Cohen, but it is also not Amanda Cohen.  No matter what happens, she should not leave this place."  Visionary looked away, and approached the portal.

"We have bigger things to worry about though, gentlemen, have you figured out how to make this work?"

The Scholar looked up, "Oh it will work, we are ready at any time, but there's a problem we can't seem to work around."

"And that is?" Nightmist asked.

Ra carefully turned, leaning on the makeshift crutch they had aquired for him, "It will only take one person at a time, and with how we are doing this, it doesn't look like we can get more than one transport without destroying the whole set-up."

"One of us, just one against Baron Blade?"  Tachyon whistled, "If only Paul was here."

"That would be ideal," Nightmist said thoughtfully, "he'd have the best shot of getting through the biggest hurdle of all."

"What's that," Unity asked.

"Convincing the people of that time to let us help them."

Anthony had lost track of time, the arguing over who would go through the portal was ongoing.  Everyone had their own reasons they should be the one to go through and try to stop Blade, only himself, Unity and Fixer were quiet.  Anthony didn't want to be left behind either, to sit here and wait, hoping some catastrophic time changes would catch up and remake his entire life.  Everyone was excited to rewrite history, to set things right and avoid this terrible state, but no one had thought about what would happen to anyone left behind.  The worst possibility was that a new timeline would come into existance, and this world would remain unchanged.  If that happened they would have no way of knowing if the mission had failed or succeeded, and Voss would still be here, furthering his testing, preparing to turn mankind into freakish soldiers for his empire.

The better option was the negation of his entire life.  That was depressing, but better than walking out of these ruins knowing tomorrow would come, dawn on a world with no hope, and only horrors awaiting it.  The people had survived, hoping and waiting for the heroes that would come and stop Voss, and now they had come, and the only hope they had brought was unmaking this world.  What were the people on the surface thinking now, now that as far as they knew all the heroes were dead, and Voss was unopposed.  Downtrodden, desperate, depressed. . .

There was power in desperation, he thought, when people have nothing to lose they won't sit back and wait for someone to help them.  "My god," he thought aloud, "did the stories keep them from fighting back?"  He resolved then and their that he would return, that this group around him could do something, they could lead this planet into war.  Maybe not a war they could win, but a war that would stop Voss from twisting and perverting this planet to his own means.  He stood up, and saw scholar standing in front of him, "Take one."  Anthony pulled a small straw out of Scholar's hand, but he wasn't thinking about that.

"Listen up guys, just because we can't all go back doesn't mean we are finished.  We're not going to sit here and hope that this world stops existing, we're going to go up and make it happen.  We can't defeat Voss and we can't save this planet, but I'll tell you what we can do, no, what we Will do.  We'll make sure that monster doesn't use a single human in his army, we'll rally the people, we'll fight on every front, to the last man, Voss may have won but we will make it his last victory, sap his resources, and die before we can be turned, he'll rue the day he ever came to our planet!"

Everyone was looking at him, and he could tell he had gotten through to them.  But they were all looking at his hand.  He looked down, saw the straw in his hand, then looked at everyone else.  He had the short straw.
